newsitem.title: UK: Canning, ex-Burson-Marsteller, opens virtual firm.
newsitem.headline: Canning, ex-Burson-Marsteller, opens virtual firm.

text.p: Alison Canning, former chief executive of public relations company Burson-Marsteller London, said on Tuesday she was setting up a "virtual" management consultancy specialising in communications.
Canning left Burson-Marsteller in October following a restructuring of the company which wiped out her job function.

She said the new company -- called First & 42nd -- would offer clients advice on corporate and brand strategy, manage corporate reputation, deal with crisis management and help companies with internal communications.
Canning has chosen to set up a management consultancy rather than a PR company because "company boards are realising that communications are core".

"Many PR companies are not intellectually robust enough to compete with management consultancies on strategy and not many of the management consultancies specialise in communications so there is a gap in the market," she told Reuters.
The company is already working on projects for drinks giant IDV and for Price Waterhouse.

Canning said that the name First & 42nd "has no real significance" beyond the fact that in the cult sci-fi novel "The Hitchhikers Guide to the Galaxy" by Douglas Adams, 42 is the answer to the meaning of life.
The company will run as a "virtual office" with staff working from home or their own offices and communicating via the Internet and internal corporate networks or "intranets".
Canning says that as the company grows it will set up a facility for "hot desking" and video conferencing.

Canning has recruited Jane Atkin, formerly director of research and planning at Burson-Marsteller, to take on the same role at First & 42nd. Canning said that she expects the company to grow to 10 or 12 people in its first year and may grow to a "couple of hundred people" in the future.
